summary: Egress transit provider dropping 'fragmentation-needed' ICMP causing large HTTP/2 model-shard streams to stall in private deploy
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent stalls when streaming large model shard downloads and long-lived gRPC/http2 connections from their Private deployment. The problem started after an on-prem network change from their transit provider two days ago.

Impact:
- Models fail to fully stream for larger shards (>64KB) causing inference requests to stall and time out after ~30s.
- Affects production traffic for FinData Analytics (private deployment, single VPC peered to our control plane).
- Observed in us-east-1 only.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) peered to Redwood control plane via TGW.
- Worker nodes: t3.large-equivalent instances with custom MTU 1500 by default.
- Presigned S3 artifact fetches used with range requests (HTTP/2 multiplexed).

Steps to reproduce (observed by customer):
1) Trigger a model load that requires range fetches (large model shard).
2) Observe initial TLS handshake completes. HTTP/2 connection established.
3) After a few KBs, the download stalls and the HTTP/2 stream is left in a half-open state; no further DATA frames from server are delivered.
4) Retry with smaller range window or reduce request size -> succeeds.

Observed behavior:
- tcpdump on worker shows server sending TCP segments but client stops ACKing after a certain MSS-sized segment. No ICMP "Fragmentation Needed (Type 3, Code 4)" is seen reaching the customer edge.
- When we instrumented a capture at the customer-VM side we do see an ICMP type 3 code 4 originating from the downstream router, but it disappears before reaching the customer's transit provider egress (suggesting provider filtering/rate limit).
- HTTP/2 stream state: initial SETTINGS/HEADERS exchange ok, partial DATA frames delivered, then stall; client eventually times out and triggers a reconnect.

Expected behavior:
- If path MTU requires fragmentation adjustments, ICMP "Fragmentation Needed (Type 3, Code 4)" should be delivered to endpoints so PMTU can adjust and streaming continues without stalls.

Additional logs / captures:
- Attached pcap snippets (provided by customer): "pcap_worker_side.pcap" shows server DATA up to a segment then no further ACK progression.
- Worker logs: serving-runtime reported repeated stream timeouts with code 14 (UNAVAILABLE) and downstream transport errors referencing ECONNRESET after timeouts.
- Console trace: Model shard fetch request id=shard-20260312-34 produced 0 bytes after 18s then retried and succeeded with MTU reduced.

Immediate customer workaround performed:
- Customer set worker node MTU to 1400 (temporary) — this prevented the need for ICMP fragmentation and streaming resumed successfully.

Notes:
- This only reproduces on large sequential downloads (range-based) or larger gRPC frame payloads; small requests and embeddings flows unaffected.
- The control plane auth and presigned URL generation are not implicated (we can generate working presigned URLs that still stall when path MTU issues present).
investigation_notes:
2026-03-12: Initial triage by Support (Aisha). Collected tcpdump + HTTP/2 trace. Customer confirms transit provider changed perimeter firewall/policy on 2026-03-11.
2026-03-12: SRE (Marco) requested pcap from customer and reproduced stalls by issuing range requests to the same object; pcap at worker shows missing ICMP fragments and stalled TCP sequence progression.
2026-03-13: We set up controlled repro from an EC2 in the customer's VPC and instrumented packet captures at three points: (a) worker VM, (b) customer edge router, (c) provider egress (captured by customer but provider did not provide mirrored capture). The VM saw ICMP type 3 code 4 originate from edge router; there is a gap at the provider handoff.
2026-03-13: Opened inbound ticket with customer's transit provider (ticket TP-44821) — provider response indicates they apply ICMP rate-limiting and drop some Type 3 messages under heavy NAT; they are investigating.
2026-03-14: SRE confirmed MTU-lowering on worker (1400) is an effective mitigation. We tested increasing TLS record granularity (server-side capping to 1200) and that also mitigates but requires runtime change.

Hypothesis:
- Transit provider's egress filtering/rate-limiting is preventing delivery of ICMP Fragmentation Needed messages to the customer's VMs, causing PMTU discovery to fail and resulting in a blackhole for packets larger than path MTU. HTTP/2/HTTP/2-over-TLS tends to push larger frames which triggers the failure more evident for large shard downloads.

Next steps / action items:
- SRE: Collect signed pcap evidence to include in provider escalation (assigned Marco Alvarez).
- Support: Document workaround steps for customer (MTU 1400 or server TLS record size cap).
- Customer: Keep transit provider ticket open and request allowing ICMP Type 3 Code 4 or otherwise enable PMTU transparency.
- Product: Consider adding an automatic fallback to smaller TLS record sizes for private deployments when PMTU probes fail (follow-up RFC).

resolution:
Workaround: Customer lowered worker MTU to 1400 which restored streaming. Alternative workaround: cap TLS record sizes/server-side chunking to avoid packets exceeding Path MTU.
Root cause: Provider-level ICMP (Fragmentation Needed) filtering/rate-limiting preventing PMTU discovery; provider ticket TP-44821 opened by customer.
Follow-up: SRE to push escalation to provider with signed pcap evidence. Product team to evaluate automatic TLS-record-size fallback for private deployments if PMTU probes fail.
